trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun Airport at 11:00 AM. Take the ADO public bus from the airport to the Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera) for about 100 MXN instead of a taxi. Check in early if possible or store luggage at Cancun Beach Resort and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby public beach stretch close to the hotel. Take a leisurely walk along the shoreline, get oriented with the area, and enjoy the turquoise Caribbean waters. Grab a snack from a local beachside vendor to keep costs low.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Boulevard Kukulcan in the Hotel Zone to get a feel for the area. Find a casual local taqueria or street food stand for an affordable first dinner in Cancun.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing to save money.
meals.lunch: El Fish Fritanga or a local beachside taco stand near the hotel — budget around 80–120 MXN.
meals.dinner: Tacos y Tortas El Rincon or a nearby taqueria — budget around 100–150 MXN for tacos, quesadillas, and a agua fresca.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 starts after 11:00 AM arrival. Use the ADO bus (approx. 100 MXN) to save on airport transfers. Keep the first day light as you settle in and recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day early with a visit to Playa Delfines, one of Cancun's most iconic and uncrowded free public beaches. Arrive by 8–9 AM to claim a great spot. Enjoy swimming, sunbathing, and the stunning panoramic view of the Hotel Zone lagoon and ocean. Entry is completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at Playa Delfines or explore the beach on foot. Bring your own snacks and water to avoid overpriced beachside vendors. In the late afternoon, head back to the hotel to rinse off and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take a local bus (Route 1 colectivo, about 12 MXN) to the Mercado 28 area for an authentic and affordable dinner experience surrounded by local vendors and artisan stalls.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at the hotel or grab pan dulce and coffee from a nearby panaderia for under 50 MXN.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or fruit from a local convenience store (OXXO or supermarket) to eat at the beach — budget 60–80 MXN.
meals.dinner: Mercado 28 food stalls — try cochinita pibil, sopa de lima, or fresh ceviche for 100–160 MXN total.

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a free public beach with no entry fee. Bring sunscreen, a beach towel, and plenty of water. Parking is available if you rent a car, but the Route 1 bus is the budget-friendly option.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to Akumal Bay for sea turtle snorkeling. Catch an early ADO or colectivo bus from Cancun to Akumal (approx. 90–120 MXN each way). Arrive by 8–9 AM before crowds gather. Snorkel directly from the beach in the calm, shallow bay where wild sea turtles graze on seagrass — no boat needed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling or relax on Akumal Beach. Rent basic snorkel gear on-site if needed (approx. 150–200 MXN). Explore the bay at your own pace and watch for sea turtles, rays, and colorful fish.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Cancun by colectivo. Relax at the hotel and enjoy a quiet evening. Pick up groceries from a nearby supermarket (Walmart or Chedraui) for a budget-friendly dinner in.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel or grab a torta from a local bakery before departing — budget 50–80 MXN.
meals.lunch: La Buena Vida beach bar in Akumal or a local comida corrida (set lunch menu) nearby for 120–180 MXN.
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal from Chedraui supermarket — fresh fruit, bread, deli items, and drinks for about 100–150 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Akumal is about 90 minutes south of Cancun by bus. Snorkeling directly from the beach is free; only gear rental costs extra. Go early to see the most sea turtles before crowds arrive. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at a different beach section near the hotel — explore Playa Tortugas or Playa Caracol, both free public beaches in the Hotel Zone accessible by the Route 1 bus. Enjoy swimming and people-watching in a more lively atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Ruinas del Rey archaeological site within the Hotel Zone (small entry fee approx. 70 MXN). Walk among ancient Mayan ruins right next to the beach — a unique and affordable cultural experience. Afterward, cool off with a swim at the adjacent beach area.
day_by_day.evening: Head into downtown Cancun (El Centro) via local bus for a vibrant and authentic evening. Browse the lively Parque de las Palapas, enjoy free live music on weekends, and grab street food from the surrounding vendors.

meals.breakfast: Cafe or juice stand near the hotel — chilaquiles or huevos rancheros for 80–110 MXN.
meals.lunch: Street food near Ruinas del Rey or a local loncheria — elotes, tostadas, or a comida corrida for 80–120 MXN.
meals.dinner: Parque de las Palapas food stands in El Centro — try marquesitas (Yucatecan crepes), tacos, or empanadas for 80–120 MXN total.

day_by_day.notes: Ruinas del Rey is one of the most affordable cultural sites in Cancun. The local Route 1 bus runs the full length of the Hotel Zone and into El Centro for just 12 MXN per ride — use it freely throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a full beach relaxation day back at Playa Delfines. Arrive early for the best experience. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it (or rent cheaply nearby) to explore the reef areas. Enjoy the uncrowded, natural setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or bus to a nearby cenote for a budget freshwater swim. Cenote Azul near Puerto Morelos is accessible by colectivo and charges around 100–150 MXN entry. Swim in the crystal-clear freshwater sinkhole — a quintessential Yucatan experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxed evening. Walk along the Hotel Zone lagoon side at sunset for beautiful views. Have dinner at a local seafood spot or taqueria near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt, fruit, and granola from the supermarket eaten at the hotel — budget 60 MXN.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for the cenote — sandwiches, fruit, and water from OXXO for about 80 MXN.
meals.dinner: Pescaderia El Oasis or a local mariscos (seafood) taqueria — fish tacos and ceviche tostadas for 120–180 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Cenote Azul near Puerto Morelos is one of the most affordable cenotes close to Cancun. Take the colectivo from downtown Cancun toward Puerto Morelos (approx. 30–40 MXN each way). Bring water shoes if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take one last swim at the beach nearest to the hotel. Enjoy the Caribbean sunrise and soak in the last moments of the trip. Pack up and check out of Cancun Beach Resort, storing luggage at the front desk if your flight is later.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Mercado 23 in El Centro (cheaper and more authentic than Hotel Zone shops) — pick up handmade crafts, vanilla extract, hot sauces, and local treats at budget prices. Head to the airport via ADO bus (100 MXN) in plenty of time for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cancun. Grab a final snack or meal at the airport or before boarding the bus.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a nearby cafe — enjoy a classic Mexican breakfast of eggs, beans, and tortillas for 80–120 MXN.
meals.lunch: Quick and affordable lunch at Mercado 23 food stalls — comida corrida or tacos for 80–120 MXN.
meals.dinner: Airport snack or light meal before departure — budget 100–150 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11 AM — confirm with the hotel. Mercado 23 is far cheaper for souvenirs than any Hotel Zone shop. Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for the bus ride and airport security. Total estimated daily budget: 400–600 MXN (approx. $20–30 USD) per day excluding accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange ground transportation to Cancun Beach Resort. Check-in and get settled into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: After freshening up, take a leisurely first look at the resort beach and Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera). Stroll along the beachfront, dip your toes in the Caribbean, and get oriented with the surroundings. Pick up any essentials at a nearby convenience store or pharmacy.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a mid-range restaurant close to the Hotel Zone. Try La Habichuela Downtown or a nearby seafood spot to ease into the Cancun dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at the airport before or after landing — a café sandwich or yogurt parfait to hold you over.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort's poolside bar or beach grill — fish tacos or a fresh ceviche to start the vacation right.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Parilla in the Hotel Zone — a beloved mid-range Mexican restaurant with great grilled meats, guacamole, and margaritas. Budget ~$20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight arrives at 11:00 AM, keep Day 1 low-key. Don't over-schedule — allow time for check-in delays, rest, and acclimatizing to the heat and humidity. Confirm any pre-booked excursions with the resort concierge this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Playa Delfines Beach Day — one of Cancun's most iconic and uncrowded public beaches. Arrive early (around 9:00 AM) to claim a good spot. Enjoy the stunning turquoise water, the famous Cancun sign for photos, and the open, less-commercialized atmosphere compared to hotel beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon continuing to relax at Playa Delfines or explore the nearby stretch of coastline. Rent a beach chair and umbrella from a local vendor. Take a swim in the calm Caribbean waters and soak up the sun.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to freshen up. Head out for a sunset stroll along Boulevard Kukulcan and browse the shops at La Isla Shopping Mall or Forum by the Sea for a casual evening out.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — eggs, fresh fruit, and coffee to fuel the beach day.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for the beach, or grab street tacos and fresh coconut water from vendors near Playa Delfines (~$5–8).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Labná Restaurant — an authentic Yucatecan mid-range restaurant serving cochinita pibil, sopa de lima, and regional specialties. Budget ~$18–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a public beach with free access and limited facilities. Bring sunscreen (reef-safe preferred), towels, plenty of water, and cash for beach vendors. It's located at the southern end of the Hotel Zone — about a 15-minute taxi or bus ride from most hotels.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Isla Mujeres Snorkeling & Beach Tour. Depart early (around 8:30–9:00 AM) by ferry from Puerto Juárez or Playa Tortugas. Explore the crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and coral. Snorkel at MUSA (Underwater Museum of Art) or Manchones Reef, both included in most tour packages.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, arrive on the island and explore Isla Mujeres on foot or by golf cart rental. Visit the colorful downtown streets, Playa Norte (one of Mexico's most beautiful beaches), and local artisan shops. Enjoy a long, leisurely lunch by the water.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the return ferry back to Cancun by around 5:30–6:00 PM. Relax at the resort and enjoy a quieter evening close to home.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — something light like toast, fruit, and juice.
meals.lunch: Lunch on Isla Mujeres at Playa Norte — try Mango Café or a beachfront palapa restaurant for fresh grilled fish, shrimp tacos, and cold beer. Budget ~$15–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at the resort restaurant or order room service for a relaxed recovery evening after a full day of activity.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Isla Mujeres Snorkeling & Beach Tour in advance through the resort concierge or a reputable operator. Ferry tickets are typically $10–15 round trip. Tour packages including snorkeling gear, guide, and ferry range from $45–70 per person. Bring waterproof sunscreen, a dry bag, and cash for the island.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Xel-Há All-Inclusive Snorkel Park adventure. Depart by shuttle or rental car by 8:30 AM (about 1.5 hours south of Cancun on the Riviera Maya). Upon arrival, enjoy the natural coastal inlet — snorkel through mangroves, float down lazy rivers, and explore underwater caves teeming with tropical fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Xel-Há's many attractions: cliff jumping platforms, bike trails, hammocks over the water, and relaxing in natural freshwater cenotes. The all-inclusive package covers food, drinks, and equipment, so take full advantage throughout the day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by shuttle around 5:30–6:30 PM. Rest at the resort and enjoy a calm evening — perhaps a walk on the resort beach at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before the early departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch is included in the Xel-Há all-inclusive package — enjoy fresh seafood, tropical fruits, Mexican dishes, and unlimited non-alcoholic drinks at the park's restaurants.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Harry's Steakhouse & Raw Bar in the Hotel Zone — a mid-to-upscale option for a special evening meal after a big adventure day. Budget ~$30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Xel-Há all-inclusive tickets typically range from $80–110 per person when booked in advance online (cheaper than at the gate). The park is located near Tulum — confirm shuttle pickup times with your tour operator or resort. Wear water shoes if possible, and bring a change of clothes for the ride back.

day_by_day.morning: Akumal Bay Sea Turtle Snorkeling excursion. Depart by 8:00 AM for the 1.5-hour drive south to Akumal Bay (near Tulum). Snorkel in the calm, shallow bay where wild sea turtles graze on seagrass just meters from shore. Rent snorkel gear locally (~$10–15) or bring your own. Arrive early for the best turtle sightings before tour groups crowd the bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Akumal, stop at a nearby cenote for a refreshing swim — Cenote Dos Ojos or Gran Cenote are both close by and spectacular. Explore the crystal-clear freshwater sinkholes, a uniquely Yucatecan experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by late afternoon. End the trip with the Sunset Catamaran Cruise — sail along the Caribbean coastline as the sun sets over the lagoon. Enjoy open bar, snacks, and music aboard the catamaran for a magical final evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the drive south.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Akumal village at La Buena Vida or a local taqueria — fresh seafood, ceviche, and cold drinks. Budget ~$12–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Light dinner after the catamaran cruise — street tacos or a casual meal at a local spot near the Hotel Zone marina. Budget ~$10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Akumal Bay has entry fees and requires snorkelers to wear life jackets (provided on-site). Book the Sunset Catamaran Cruise in advance as spots fill quickly — prices range from $55–85 per person including open bar. This is a full and action-packed day, so pace yourself and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cancun — enjoy a slow, relaxed breakfast at the resort. Take one last swim in the Caribbean or lounge by the pool. Pack your bags and check out of the resort. Store luggage with the concierge if your flight is in the afternoon or evening.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your final afternoon browsing the Mercado 28 (local artisan market) for souvenirs — hammocks, pottery, Mayan crafts, vanilla, and local snacks. Practice your bargaining skills for the best prices. Alternatively, visit a nearby cenote or simply relax on the hotel beach one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport with plenty of time before your departure flight. Enjoy a final meal at the airport or a nearby restaurant before flying home.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — treat yourself to a proper sit-down meal with eggs, fresh tropical fruit, pastries, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado 28 or a nearby local restaurant — try a traditional Yucatecan dish like sopa de lima or poc chuc as a farewell meal. Budget ~$10–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a quick farewell meal near the Hotel Zone before departure — keep it light and easy for travel.

day_by_day.notes: Cancun International Airport is about 20–30 minutes from the Hotel Zone. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security. Use any remaining Mexican pesos on food, drinks, or last-minute gifts at the market or airport shops. Confirm your flight check-in online the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Cancun Beach Resort. Check-in, unpack, and settle into your premium suite. Enjoy a welcome cocktail and orientation tour of the resort facilities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the resort's private beach for your first taste of the Caribbean. Relax on a premium sun lounger with personalized beach butler service. Take a leisurely swim in the turquoise waters and explore the beachfront at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's rooftop bar overlooking the Caribbean Sea. Enjoy the golden hour views as you decompress from travel.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light bite at the airport before landing
meals.lunch: La Fisheria — upscale seafood restaurant in the Hotel Zone with fresh ceviche and grilled fish with stunning lagoon views
meals.dinner: Tempo by Daniel Boulud at the Paradisus Cancun — Michelin-pedigree French-Mediterranean cuisine with an exceptional wine list; reserve in advance

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day is intentionally relaxed. Pre-arrange airport fast-track immigration and private transfer for a seamless luxury arrival experience. Confirm dinner reservations upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Playa Delfines Beach Day — Head to one of Cancun's most iconic and uncrowded public beaches for a premium morning experience. Arrive early to secure the best stretch of shoreline. Playa Delfines offers dramatic open-ocean views, powerful waves, and a stunning backdrop of the Hotel Zone skyline. Bring a private picnic setup arranged by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a luxurious spa session at the resort's premium wellness center. Indulge in a 90-minute Caribbean hot stone massage or a couples' hydrotherapy treatment. Follow with a private pool cabana session with dedicated service.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Catamaran Cruise — Board a private or small-group luxury catamaran along the Caribbean coastline. Watch the sun dip below the lagoon horizon with open bar service, premium canapés, and live acoustic music. Approximately 2 hours on the water.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast butler service — fresh tropical fruit platter, eggs Benedict, fresh-squeezed juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside gourmet picnic curated by the resort chef — chilled lobster rolls, artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and sparkling water at Playa Delfines
meals.dinner: Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar — one of Cancun's finest steakhouses in the Hotel Zone, celebrated for USDA prime cuts, fresh oysters, and an award-winning wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sunset Catamaran Cruise in advance as premium private charters fill quickly. Ask the concierge to arrange a seamless beach-to-spa-to-cruise flow for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Isla Mujeres Snorkeling & Beach Tour — Take a private or premium ferry to the charming island of Isla Mujeres. Explore the crystal-clear waters teeming with vibrant marine life including tropical fish, rays, and coral formations. A private guided snorkeling excursion ensures personalized attention and the best underwater spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Isla Mujeres village on a private golf cart tour. Visit Punta Sur, the island's dramatic southern cliff with panoramic Caribbean views. Spend leisure time at Playa Norte, consistently rated one of the world's most beautiful beaches, with calm turquoise shallows perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return by private ferry to Cancun at sunset. Freshen up at the resort before a refined evening out.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant — avocado toast with smoked salmon, tropical fruit bowls, and freshly brewed Mexican coffee
meals.lunch: Olivia Restaurant on Isla Mujeres — beloved Mediterranean-Caribbean fusion spot with fresh catch of the day, hummus platters, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Lorenzillo's — iconic Cancun waterfront restaurant built over the lagoon, renowned for live lobster, premium seafood, and an unmatched romantic ambiance

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a private boat charter for the Isla Mujeres trip rather than the public ferry for the ultimate luxury experience — includes snorkeling gear, onboard refreshments, and a dedicated guide.

day_by_day.morning: Akumal Bay Sea Turtle Snorkeling — Take a private luxury transfer south along the Riviera Maya to Akumal Bay (approximately 1.5 hours from Cancun). Snorkel in the calm, shallow bay where wild sea turtles graze on seagrass just meters from the shoreline. A private certified marine biologist guide enhances the experience with fascinating ecological insights.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Akumal, visit the nearby Tulum Ruins for a scenic and culturally enriching stop. The clifftop Mayan ruins overlooking the Caribbean offer breathtaking photo opportunities and historical context. Private guided tour recommended for a deeper experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun via private transfer. Unwind at the resort with a private beachfront yoga or meditation session arranged at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast box prepared by the resort — croissants, fresh fruit, yogurt parfait, and cold brew coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Cetli Restaurant in Tulum — celebrated for authentic Oaxacan cuisine using traditional techniques; try the mole negro with duck and handmade tortillas
meals.dinner: La Habichuela Downtown — a Cancun institution since 1977, serving elevated Yucatecan and Caribbean cuisine in a magical garden setting; must-try cocobichuela (lobster and shrimp in coconut curry sauce)

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest travel day of the itinerary. Depart by 7:30 AM to arrive at Akumal before the crowds. The private transfer makes the journey comfortable and flexible. Confirm Tulum Ruins entry tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Xel-Há All-Inclusive Snorkel Park — Journey to this extraordinary natural aquatic theme park built around a stunning coastal inlet. Snorkel through mangrove channels, cenotes, and open coves bursting with tropical fish and natural beauty. Upgrade to the premium all-inclusive package for cliff jumping, snuba diving, and bike trails through the jungle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Xel-Há at a leisurely pace. Relax in the natural lazy river, enjoy the hammocks over the water, or book a premium snuba dive for a deeper underwater experience. The park's natural freshwater-saltwater mixing zone creates a uniquely diverse ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a premium beach bonfire experience arranged by the concierge — private stretch of beach, fire pit, premium spirits, and a private chef preparing fresh ceviche and grilled seafood tableside.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — extensive spread including made-to-order omelets, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and Mexican specialties
meals.lunch: All-inclusive gourmet lunch at Xel-Há — fresh seafood stations, grilled meats, tropical salads, and unlimited premium beverages included in the park package
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire dinner at the resort — personalized 4-course menu by the resort chef featuring fresh local catch, grilled lobster, and a decadent chocolate lava cake finale under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Book the premium Xel-Há package well in advance as it includes additional activities and priority access. The private beach dinner is the highlight of the trip — coordinate with the concierge at least 48 hours ahead to ensure flawless execution.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a slow, indulgent start to the day. Take one last swim in the Caribbean, stroll the beach at sunrise, or book a final spa treatment. Visit the resort's infinity pool for a peaceful morning session with a signature cocktail or fresh juice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping along Avenida Kukulcán in the Hotel Zone for premium souvenirs, Mexican artisan goods, and luxury resort wear. Visit La Isla Shopping Village for designer boutiques and waterfront dining. Pack, check out, and arrange private luxury transfer to Cancun International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparation — enjoy the resort's premium checkout experience with late checkout if available. Private transfer to the airport with ample time for premium lounge access before your departing flight.

meals.breakfast: Farewell champagne breakfast on your private suite balcony — eggs royale, smoked salmon blinis, fresh tropical fruits, mimosas, and specialty Mexican coffee
meals.lunch: Puerto Madero — Argentine-inspired steakhouse in the Hotel Zone with premium cuts, fresh pasta, and a world-class wine selection for a memorable farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or early dinner at the resort before transfer — light but elegant bites to keep energy up for travel

day_by_day.notes: Request late checkout (typically until 2:00–4:00 PM) through the concierge to maximize your final day without feeling rushed. Confirm private transfer timing based on your departure flight. Keep one carry-on accessible for any last-minute beach or pool essentials on the final morning.

query: Cancun beach resort, $3000 couple, 6 days, March 2027, from Dallas
